title: Create scalable luminance token map and hierarchy for dense tables and compact components
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define a luminance-driven color token map and a compressed token hierarchy for high-density table surfaces, inline controls, and chart overlays. The goal is to improve perceived contrast in small UI elements without increasing visual noise, simplify CSS variable usage for engineering, and provide a migration plan that preserves existing visuals where customers rely on them.

Scope:
- Surface tokens: neutral and accent luminance anchors tuned for 10–18px UI contexts (table rows, action chips, badges).
- Typography scale: minor rebaseline for caption and label sizes to improve legibility at small sizes while staying backwards compatible for headings and body text.
- Spacing & radius: introduce a compact radius scale (2px/4px/6px) for dense tables and maintain the existing default scale for panels.
- Shadow/elevation: create a reduced-penumbra micro-shadow set optimized for small elements to avoid heavy-looking drop shadows at compact sizes.
- Migration: automated token aliases, a runtime compatibility aliasing layer in CSS/variables, and a staged rollout with a console feature flag.

Non-goals: overhauling global color system or redesigning major components (those are follow-ups). This ticket focuses on the token layer and a small set of affected components (Table, DataGrid row, Compact Button, Mini-Pill).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Luminance-first tokens: We prioritize absolute luminance steps rather than perceptual hue-preserving deltas. This reduces edge-case contrast regressions in small controls, but slightly constrains expressive accent variations.
- Compact radius choices: 2/4/6px are chosen to map well to pixel grids on low-DPI screens; this may look tight on high-DPI devices but will be reconciled in a follow-up responsive token ticket.
- Micro-shadows vs no shadow: Adding micro-shadows improves element separation in dense tables, but raises concerns about printed/exported views; classification into print-safe tokens will be included in docs.

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: Confluence - /spaces/UX/pages/Redwood/Compact+Token+Map+PRD (internal)
- Figma exploration frames: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/compact-token-map
- GitHub starter draft for CSS variables and token aliases: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/2245
- Visual regression dashboard: https://kuboard.internal/reports/token-map-compact-2025-03-07

Acceptance criteria:
- Token spec published in design tokens repo (JSON + human-readable MD).
- Engineering implementation provides CSS variables for new tokens and aliases for legacy tokens.
- Automated visual diffs for the impacted components show <= 6% pixel delta for primary customers flagged as conservative.
- Console rollout flag implemented and QA checklist completed.

Next steps:
1) Finalize luminance anchors and micro-shadow values with research (contrast pairs + user testing on small type sizes).
2) Ship token JSON and minimal CSS variable shims.
3) Implement feature-flagged rollout for select internal tenants.
4) Track regressions and iterate.

Risks and mitigations:
- Customer regressions: include alias layer and opt-out tokens to revert visual changes quickly.
- Cross-platform mismatch: add integration tests across browsers and high/low DPI contexts.
- Accessibility: enforce AA contrast for label/caption pairs; escalate to accessibility review if we find issues.
comments: 2025-03-05 — Maya Chen: Kicked off exploration with two luminance scaffolds; team prefers absolute luminance anchors (L20/L30/L45) to avoid hue clipping in small UI contexts. Shared Figma frames and PRD draft.

2025-03-06 — Design review: Jorge (Eng) asked for simpler aliasing strategy so runtime doesn't need token transforms. Decided on 1:1 CSS variable aliases for six legacy tokens to be maintained for 2 releases.

2025-03-07 — Research: Quick contrast audit against the default palette across eight small-size label combinations. Found three combos below AA; updated anchors and rechecked. Results posted to visual regression dashboard.
2025-03-09 — PM feedback (Ava Patel): Requested migration plan that splits rollout by customer tier and includes a rollback plan tied to console feature flags. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-10 — Engineering sync: Liam O. and Priya S. confirmed the variable shingles and provided initial PR for CSS variables (PR #2245). Agreed on micro-shadow CSS tokens: shadow-compact-1/2/3.
2025-03-11 — Design sign-off: I signed off on the token values pending accessibility audit. Next: tag security/compliance only if printing/export contexts show regressions.
